neighbours.label: the predicate of acquaintance or connection ('familiar', 'acquainted', 'linked') that expects a with/to complement
fire: By the second week the new recruits were familiar with the alarm codes.
Few readers today are acquainted with his early poems.
Researchers say the gene has been linked to a higher risk of asthma.
The farmers in the valley are quite familiar with sudden floods.
My grandmother was personally acquainted with the old mayor.
Smoking is strongly linked to heart disease in older adults.
Anyone familiar with the software can fix the problem in minutes.
The town's name is closely linked to the salt trade.
quiet: By the second week the new recruits were tired of the alarm drills.
Few readers today are fond of his early poems.
Researchers say the gene has been found in a group of asthma patients.
The farmers in the valley are quite worried about sudden floods.
My grandmother was personally invited by the old mayor.
Smoking is strongly discouraged for older adults with heart disease.
Anyone patient enough can fix the software problem in minutes.
The town's name comes from the old salt trade.

notes: card top: linked, familiar, direct, nothing; probe: familiar/acquainted ~0.5, linked 0.35, 'have to' and 'no interest' ~0.
